title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 25, 2026
summary: Nicaragua's Ortega-aligned National Assembly approved a reform on August 24 extending the mandates of 6,320 municipal officials — 153 mayors, 153 vice-mayors, and 6,014 councilmembers — to seven years, canceling the municipal elections that had been scheduled for 2026. The FSLN currently governs all 153 municipalities, and municipal employees and analysts say the reform removes any mechanism for citizens to hold local authorities accountable, extending a pattern that began with 2025's 'Chamuca' reform. The days-since-election-ban KPI was updated to 37, and a new claim captures the government's institutional-continuity framing against critics' accountability concerns.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Senators Ted Cruz (R-TX) and Tim Kaine (D-VA) introduced a bipartisan bill, the Restoring Electoral Fairness and Opposition Rights through Mandates for Accountability Act, renewing and expanding sanctions on Ortega-Murillo regime officials and newly targeting Nicaragua's gold sector and entities aiding Russia and Iran. The bill builds on Cruz's 2018 NICA Act and conditions sanctions relief on free and fair elections. It follows the OAS's August 19 vote to convene an emergency foreign ministers' session over Ortega's declaration ending elections. Added Sen. Cruz to the political figures tracked and updated the days-since-election-ban KPI to 33.
